sds-purpose-access.title: Purpose of Safety Data Sheets and Employee Access
sds-purpose-access.content: A Safety Data Sheet is one of the most important tools for understanding hazardous chemicals. It tells employees what the material is, what hazards it presents, how to respond in an emergency, and what precautions are required. Under OSHA's Hazard Communication Standard (29 CFR 1910.1200), employees must have access to SDSs for all hazardous chemicals in their work area. SDSs are valuable tools for all workers — not just safety professionals.

sds-sections-1-2.title: SDS Sections 1–2: Identification and Hazard Identification
sds-sections-1-2.content: GHS-compliant SDSs contain 16 standardized numbered sections. Section 1 (Identification) provides the product name and the manufacturer's or distributor's name, address, phone number, and emergency contact. Section 2 (Hazard Identification) describes all hazards of the chemical and includes required label elements: signal word, hazard statements, precautionary statements, and pictograms. These two sections are the quickest way to determine what a chemical is and what its primary hazards are.

sds-sections-3-5.title: SDS Sections 3–5: Composition, First Aid, Firefighting
sds-sections-3-5.content: Section 3 (Composition/Ingredients) lists chemical components. Section 4 (First-Aid Measures) provides instructions for initial care after exposure, including eye contact, skin contact, inhalation, and ingestion — essential information for emergency response. Section 5 (Firefighting Measures) identifies suitable extinguishing agents, hazards from combustion, and protective equipment for firefighters. These sections are critical during emergency response.

sds-sections-6-8.title: SDS Sections 6–8: Accidental Release, Handling/Storage, Exposure Controls/PPE
sds-sections-6-8.content: Section 6 (Accidental Release Measures) provides procedures for spills, leaks, and uncontrolled releases — including personal precautions, containment, cleanup, and disposal. Section 7 (Handling and Storage) describes safe handling practices and storage requirements, including incompatibilities. Section 8 (Exposure Controls/PPE) lists occupational exposure limits, engineering controls, and required personal protective equipment such as gloves, respirators, and eye protection.

sds-sections-9-12.title: SDS Sections 9–12: Physical Properties, Stability, Toxicology, Environmental
sds-sections-9-12.content: Section 9 (Physical and Chemical Properties) covers appearance, odor, pH, flammability, and vapor pressure. Section 10 (Stability and Reactivity) addresses chemical stability, reactivity conditions, and materials to avoid — critical when storing chemicals near one another. Section 11 (Toxicological Information) describes routes of exposure and health effects. Section 12 (Ecological Information) addresses environmental impact of a release.

sds-sections-13-16.title: SDS Sections 13–16: Disposal, Transport, Regulatory, Other
sds-sections-13-16.content: Section 13 (Disposal Considerations) guides safe disposal of the chemical and contaminated materials. Section 14 (Transport Information) provides UN numbers, proper shipping names, and transport classifications. Section 15 (Regulatory Information) lists applicable safety, health, and environmental regulations. Section 16 (Other Information) may include revision dates, key abbreviations, or references. These sections support regulatory compliance, disposal, and long-term chemical management.

sds-workplace-use.title: Using SDSs Effectively in the Workplace
sds-workplace-use.content: Before working with a hazardous chemical, review its SDS. Confirm the product identifier matches the container label. Know the hazards, required PPE, storage requirements, first-aid steps, spill procedures, and emergency contact information. Know where SDSs are kept in your work area. If you cannot understand SDS information, or cannot find the SDS for a chemical, stop work and ask a supervisor or safety professional. Never guess — chemical safety depends on preparation and access to information.
